text:
maria: quick follow-up from the GQA/MQA attention kernel RFC thread. ran a few mixed-workload probes this week and seeing a corner case where the selector flips to GQA and increases p95 by ~30ms for small groups. notes below — want opinions on changing the selector boundary vs adding a latency override flag

kiran: curious — is this happening for short sequences or high fanout?

maria: short sequences (avg_seq ~ 24), group sizes 2-5, high variance in tokenization. throughput is fine, but p95 spikes when GQA picks a kernel that assumes larger SIMD-friendly batches. cost goes down slightly but tail latency regresses.

tara: do you have the selector decision trace? maybe fallback logic isn't triggering because affinity metadata looks compatible but actual microshape isn't.

maria: pasted an anonymized trace: 
```
selector: group_id=bb1, candidate_kernels=[gqa_fused_v3, mqa_prefetch_v2],
choice: gqa_fused_v3 (score 0.72)
observed: avg_batch=3, seq=24, kv_cache_hit=0.12, latency=120ms (p95)
fallback: none (no capacity pressure)
```

maria: the score comes from our heuristic: kernel_score = perf_est(seq, batch) * affinity_weight - cost_penalty. But perf_est is overfitted to larger batches.

aj: hmm. two options: 1) move microshape-aware checks into the selector (i.e., inspect avg_batch and seq before scoring), or 2) add a lightweight signal to kernels: can_handle_small_group = true/false and short-circuit. My vote: make kernels advertise explicit microshape capabilities — keeps selector simpler.

leo: advertising capability + a soft override seems nice. if kernel advert says `small_group_ok=false`, selector can drop it early. also add a `latency_safe_mode` flag per request that prefers low tail latency at a small cost increase.

tara: is there risk of exploding kernel matrix size? we already have many kernel variants per quant/arch/seq. adding boolean caps seems cheap though.

maria: agreed — boolean capability keys keep combinatorics manageable: small_group_ok, short_seq_ok, kv_sparse_ok. then selector flow becomes: filter kernels by required capabilities -> score remaining. fewer bad picks.

aj: small implementation sketch: 
```
# pseudocode for selector loop
req_caps = request.runtime_caps + client_slo_caps
cands = [k for k in kernel_catalog if req_caps subset_of k.capabilities]
best = argmax(cands, lambda k: score(k, workload_stats))
```

maria: experiment results after adding a simple `small_group_ok` filter in the probe branch: p95 drops ~28ms for these cases, cost delta +2%. Seems acceptable.

leo: do we need an opt-in config in Dedicated/Private? i.e., default to safety for hosted customers but allow dedicated to tune for cost.

maria: for hosted we can default `latency_safe_mode=false` but have a global feature flag for safety in the short term. For Dedicated, expose a config toggle per model route.

tara: what about rollouts? canary on a single region, 1% traffic, then ramp. we should track p50/p95/cost per-model and have regression alarms.

maria: yep — will add canary plan to RFC follow-up. also need to update the kernel catalog schema: add `capabilities: ["small_group_ok","short_seq_ok","kv_sparse_ok"]` and `preferred_workloads` free text.

aj: tiny nit — prefer `capabilities` be a set of short tokens (no free text) and `metadata` blob for free text; easier to query.

infra-bot: deploy plan created: attention-selector/capability-filtering v0.1 -> canary in us-west-2 at 1% traffic, schedule 2026-03-25T22:00Z

maria: thanks. next steps: 1) PR to kernel-catalog schema (aj), 2) selector filter patch + tests (kiran), 3) canary metrics dashboard (leo), 4) docs + rollout steps (tara). I'll put items on the RFC follow-up doc and ping owners. :thumbsup:

kiran: I'll start the selector patch tomorrow, will add unit tests that simulate microshape mismatch cases.

leo: I'll stub a dashboard with p50/p95/cost and add an annotation for canary start.

maria: awesome — feel free to ping me for infra quotas if canary needs extra capacity. thanks all :party_parrot:
